findings.title: AgentCore harness: unvalidated caller-controlled model configuration allows SigV4 credential redirection and `Authorization` header override
findings.description: `InvokeHarness` accepts a `model` object whose `additionalParams` are, in AWS's words, "passed through to the underlying model provider unchanged. The harness does not validate, filter, or restrict these parameters." Any principal that can influence that field can set LiteLLM's `aws_bedrock_runtime_endpoint` to route the **signed request, including the SigV4 signature and session credentials**, to an attacker-chosen endpoint; set OpenAI's `extra_headers` to inject or override the outbound `Authorization` header; set `aws_role_name` to attempt assumption of a different IAM role (bounded only by whether the execution role holds `sts:AssumeRole`); or set `modelId`/`apiBase` to silently redirect inference to a different model, region or provider. AWS offers no server-side control — every suggested mitigation is customer-side input validation. This is a first-class prompt-injection and credential-exfiltration target: an agent that forwards any part of caller-supplied JSON into `InvokeHarness` hands over its model routing and its credentials. AIRT must add harness `additionalParams`/`apiBase`/`modelId` manipulation to its automated test surface; AISPM must flag harnesses reachable by untrusted callers that do not strip the `model` field, and execution roles carrying `sts:AssumeRole`

findings.title: AgentCore harness: per-invocation `skills` override is an arbitrary instruction-injection channel
findings.description: Skills are markdown-plus-script bundles the harness fetches from S3 or Git **at invocation time** and injects directly into the agent's context. AWS states the harness "treats all skill content as trusted input. It does not validate, sanitize, or inspect the content or source of skills before providing them to the agent" — and that "skills can be overridden per `InvokeHarness` call." The combination means a caller who reaches `InvokeHarness` can point the agent at their own S3 prefix or Git repo and supply the agent's instructions and executable scripts wholesale, bypassing whatever skill set the harness was configured with at the control plane. The configured-skills view in any inventory is therefore **not** an accurate picture of what actually ran. AIRT should treat skill-source substitution as a distinct attack primitive from prompt injection; AISPM must inventory each harness's configured skill sources, alert when a skill source is an S3 bucket or Git repo outside the account's trust boundary, and treat "skills not stripped from caller input" as a toxic combination with any externally reachable harness endpoint

findings.title: AgentCore harness is invisible as a distinct resource type in CloudTrail
findings.description: AWS documents that "in CloudTrail, harness resources appear under the `AWS::BedrockAgentCore::Runtime` resource type rather than a harness-specific type," and that data-plane calls are logged as `InvokeAgentRuntime`, `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` and `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell` — **`InvokeHarness` never appears as a CloudTrail event name**. A harness invocation is therefore indistinguishable by event name from a plain AgentCore Runtime invocation, and control-plane events carry the harness ARN in `resources.ARN` while data-plane events carry the *runtime* ARN, so the two halves of a harness's audit trail do not join on a common identifier without an externally maintained harness→runtime mapping. Compounding this, harness traces only exist if **Transaction Search is enabled in CloudWatch (a one-time, per-account opt-in)** and the execution role carries the logs/X-Ray statements — so an account can run harnesses with no trace data at all and no error. AIDR must build the harness→runtime ARN mapping from control-plane events and use it to attribute data-plane activity, must not rely on a `harness` resource type existing, and should alert when a harness exists in an account where Transaction Search is off

findings.title: AgentCore harness IAM: `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell` is the one invoke API that does not require `InvokeAgentRuntime`
findings.description: The newly published harness permissions table shows every harness API requiring permissions on both the harness resource and the underlying Runtime resource — `InvokeHarness` needs `InvokeHarness` **and** `InvokeAgentRuntime`, `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` needs its own action **and** `InvokeAgentRuntime`, and Create/Update/Delete each additionally require the matching `*AgentRuntime` **and** `*Memory` actions. `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell` requires only `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell`. A least-privilege policy written around `InvokeAgentRuntime` — the obvious chokepoint, and the one most existing AWS guidance names — therefore does **not** gate interactive shell access to the microVM, the highest-capability path into a harness session (persistent shells, 256 KB replayable buffered output, up to 10 concurrent shells, reported 2026-09-23). AISPM must add the two new ARN shapes (`.../harness/<id>` and `.../harness/<id>/harness-endpoint/<name>`) as inventory resource types, evaluate harness policies against the full 14-row action table rather than against Runtime actions alone, and raise a finding on any principal holding `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell` without a corresponding `InvokeHarness` grant — that combination is shell access without the ability to use the agent normally

findings.title: ServiceNow Brazil (EA 2026-09-24) adds Autonomous Engineer — an unattended agent that builds and deploys ServiceNow applications
findings.description: A new ServiceNow release family is current, and its headline new entity is **Autonomous Engineer**: an agent that "runs on Build Agent and uses the same skills" but is explicitly designed for work handed off with "nobody... to sit and watch it happen." It is gated behind a **new AI Workflow Factory SKU** on top of Brazil EA, so its presence is separately entitled and separately detectable. The capability it inherits from Build Agent is the concerning part: full-stack application authoring across tables, flows, UI and scripts, **generating and executing** ATF test scenarios, and **deploying via update sets** — all "restricted to admin-level permissions only." An unattended, admin-privileged, natural-language-driven agent that emits promotable update sets is a code-to-production path with no human in the loop, and it composes with the global-scope authoring capability reported on 2026-09-18. Brazil also adds **Skills** and **Rules** as new Build Agent organizing constructs, six **playbook** changes including generate-and-deploy-as-a-unit, five new **Fluent/Now SDK** APIs (`RestMessage`, `Alias`, `AliasTemplate`, `RetryPolicy`, `DataLookup`) with domain-separation support and CI/CD CLI — `RestMessage` as a Fluent-declarable API means an agent-authored definition can create outbound HTTP integrations as code — and a redesigned **AI Agent Studio** that versions a combined agent/tool/workflow definition and emits update sets for promotion. AISPM needs Autonomous Engineer runs as an inventory and activity entity distinct from Build Agent sessions, the Skills/Rules constructs as the policy objects that constrain them, the AI Workflow Factory entitlement as a discovery signal, and update-set promotion as a provenance surface answering "which agent authored the code now running in production."

findings.title: Dia Browser writes to Notion and aggregates across four governed systems into one document
findings.description: Dia 1.47.1 adds Notion as the first connected tool that is a **write destination** rather than a read source, and pairs it with cross-tool fan-out: a single natural-language request reads Slack DMs, email threads and Google Docs and concentrates the result into a Notion page. The vendor's own worked example is an employee performance dossier — "find me conversations where Susan's communication and leadership skills excelled this Summer, collecting it all in a Notion doc." This extends the Dia connector finding reported 2026-09-27 in a materially different direction: data does not just enter the browser, it leaves it into a fifth system, assembled client-side from four separately governed sources, with no DLP, retention or eDiscovery control in the path and no authorization model, admin control or audit surface documented on the release note. ENDPOINT must enumerate Dia tool connections including their direction (read vs. write) and treat a write-capable connector as an egress channel; AISPM should register the resulting Notion grant as a third-party app consent on the Notion workspace

platforms.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
details: **Lifecycle hook decision semantics and 64 KiB context truncation** — the `harness-lifecycle-hooks` page was audited in full for the first time. Beyond the four hook points reported on 2026-09-22, the page documents that only a **Lambda** target can change agent-loop behavior (SNS and EventBridge are notification-only and their `hookEvent` "does not confirm that the target received the event"); that each hook `context` object is capped at **64 KiB**, after which the harness silently replaces the largest fields with `{"truncated": true, "preview": "..."}` and — AWS's own words — "**Context truncation does not activate `failureMode`**"; that a `before_tool_call` decision "controls execution, not visibility in the stream"; that an `after_tool_call` deny "**does not remove the completed tool result**"; and that `UpdateHarness` with a `hooks` list **replaces the entire existing configuration**, with an empty list removing every hook. Max 20 hooks per harness; Lambda `failureMode` is selectable `deny` (default) or `allow`. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness-lifecycle-hooks.html

platforms.name: Dia Browser

It ships a **Microsoft tool suite** — Outlook (email and calendar), Teams (channel messages, thread analysis, meeting chat) and SharePoint (document changes and content) — feeding a "Morning Brief" surface, alongside existing Slack support now extended to voice-note transcripts and screenshot reading. findings.title: Dia Browser "Tools" — enterprise SaaS connector surface in a consumer AI browser
findings.description: Dia 1.49.0 turns the browser into a multi-tenant connector host. Tools now read **Outlook mail and calendar, Teams channel/thread/meeting-chat messages, SharePoint documents, Slack (including voice-note transcripts and screenshots)**, and in beta **Zoom recordings/transcripts, Salesforce accounts/contacts/leads/cases/opportunities, Figma files and comments, and Canva designs**. This is corporate mail, meeting audio and CRM data flowing into an AI browser that sits outside every Microsoft, Salesforce and Zoom governance control Zenity already maps — and it is installed by end users, not admins. New entity types to inventory: Dia tool connections, their grant scopes, the per-user OAuth consents they create against M365/Salesforce/Zoom/Slack tenants, and the "Morning Brief" aggregation surface that concatenates them. ENDPOINT must detect Dia installs and enumerate connected tools; AISPM should treat a Dia tool grant as a third-party app consent on the upstream tenant. The release note documents **no authorization model, no admin control and no audit surface**, and an open request channel implies the catalog will keep growing

findings.title: AgentCore harness lifecycle hooks: silent context truncation and non-authoritative hook events
findings.description: Extends the hook surface reported 2026-09-22 with mechanics that determine whether hooks can be trusted as a detection or enforcement feed. A hook's `context` is capped at **64 KiB** and the harness silently substitutes truncation markers for the largest fields — including `toolInput` and `toolResult` — and AWS states that "context truncation does not activate `failureMode`", so a gating or logging Lambda receives partial tool arguments while still being required to return a decision: **the largest (and most interesting) tool payloads are exactly the ones that arrive incomplete**. SNS and EventBridge targets cannot deny anything and their `hookEvent` "does not confirm that the target received the event", with no ordering guarantee outside an SNS FIFO topic — so a hook-based audit trail can lose events without surfacing an error. `before_tool_call` "controls execution, not visibility in the stream" (the model-generated tool request is already visible before the decision), and an `after_tool_call` deny **retains** the completed tool result. Finally, `UpdateHarness` replaces the hook list wholesale and an empty list removes all hooks, making silent de-instrumentation a single control-plane call. AIDR must ingest `hookEvent` while flagging truncation markers rather than treating hook payloads as complete; AISPM should alert on hook lists shrinking, on `failureMode: allow`, and on notification-only targets used where the customer believes they have enforcement

platforms.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
details: **`harness-tools` audited for the first time.** Documents five attachable tool types (`remote_mcp`, `agentcore_gateway`, `agentcore_browser`, `agentcore_code_interpreter`, `inline_function`) plus two always-on builtins (`shell`, `file_operations`), the `allowedTools` glob-pattern restriction language, and the credential model for each. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness-tools.html

**`harness-command-shell` audited for the first time.** The `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell` WebSocket API behind the already-reported "Harness: Interactive shells" release note — binary frame protocol, dual auth paths, detach/reconnect semantics, and the logging model. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness-command-shell.html

**Web Search Tool reachable from a harness.** Not a harness tool type — it is an AgentCore Gateway target with `connectorId: "web-search"`, surfaced to the agent as an MCP `WebSearch` tool. Requires `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch` on the Gateway service role and `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeGateway` on the harness execution role. `us-east-1` only. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness-tools.html

Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-sessions#retrieve-local-sessions

**Compliance Activity Feed no longer returns file names, project document names or artifact titles.** The `filename` and `title` fields are now always empty or omitted — retroactively, including on activities recorded before the change. findings.title: AgentCore `allowedTools` does not restrict `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` — the tool allowlist and the shell API are unrelated controls
findings.description: The `allowedTools` parameter on an AgentCore harness accepts glob patterns (`"@builtin/shell"`, `"@git/read_*"`, `"@*-mcp/status"`) and reads exactly like a sandbox. AWS states verbatim that it **"scopes LLM tool selection during `InvokeHarness` only. It does not affect `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand`, which is a separate API with its own IAM action (`bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand`) that executes commands directly without passing through the LLM."** The documented remediation is **"do not grant `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` in your IAM policies."** Per the harness-environment audit on 2026-09-25, that API runs as **root (uid 0)** in the microVM, above the container's `USER` directive. So a harness configured with `allowedTools: ["@builtin/file_operations"]` — no shell, by every reading of its configuration — is fully shell-capable to any principal holding that one IAM action. Compounding it: **omitting `allowedTools` allows all tools**, a fail-open default. AISPM must treat `allowedTools` and the `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand`/`InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell` IAM grants as **two independent controls on one harness**, and raise a toxic combination when a harness carries a restrictive `allowedTools` list *and* any principal holds either shell IAM action on it — that pairing is the signature of an operator who believes they have sandboxed an agent and has not

findings.title: AgentCore harness tool attachment — five tool types, arbitrary remote MCP by URL, and plaintext credentials in harness config
findings.description: `harness-tools` documents the full attachment surface for an AgentCore harness, each a distinct inventory entity: **`remote_mcp`** (any remote MCP endpoint by URL — AWS notes "No Gateway required for simple cases," so this path carries **no Gateway policy enforcement, no inbound/outbound auth and no access control**), **`agentcore_gateway`** (governed, policy-backed, by ARN — with outbound auth selectable as AWS IAM, **None**, or OAuth), **`agentcore_browser`**, **`agentcore_code_interpreter`**, and **`inline_function`**. Two builtins — **`shell`** (bash) and **`file_operations`** (view/create/edit) — are present in **every session** unless restricted. Critically, a `remote_mcp` tool's `headers` map holds **raw plaintext secrets**: AWS's own example is `{"Authorization": "Bearer <your-token>"}`, with the Token Vault reference syntax (`${arn:...:apikeycredentialprovider/...}`) offered only as the better alternative. Tools are settable at **CreateHarness, UpdateHarness and per-`InvokeHarness`** — so a create-time inventory snapshot does not describe what the agent actually had at runtime. AISPM must inventory harness tools as first-class entities, flag `remote_mcp` targets pointing outside the org's approved MCP set, flag literal credential material in `headers`, and flag `agentcore_gateway` tools whose outbound auth is `None`

findings.title: AgentCore interactive shells: full terminal access with a documented command-content logging blind spot, plus a shell-takeover primitive
findings.description: The `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell` WebSocket API opens a persistent bash terminal inside the harness session's microVM. AWS states a principal holding it **"has interactive command access to the harness session"** and that the shell **"can access customer-provided data, files, and secrets in the selected environment or on mounted filesystems"** and reach any network destination the session can. The audit surface is the problem: **"The service doesn't log terminal input or output"** to CloudWatch, and **"CloudTrail doesn't log terminal input or output"** either — CloudTrail records only caller identity, timestamp, source IP and response status for the *connection*. Every command run against mounted EFS or bidirectionally-synced S3 filesystems is therefore invisible. Two further surfaces: authentication has a **second path that evaluates no IAM action at all** (bearer-token requests "must satisfy the harness inbound authorizer instead," with the token carried inside a `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` value for browser clients); and **opening a second connection with the same `shellId` replaces the first**, evicting the original client with close code `4000` while the shell's environment, working directory and running processes persist — a session-takeover primitive against a live agent terminal. Detached shells keep running and do not count toward the 10-active-shell limit. AIDR must add shell-connection events as an activity type keyed on `shellId` + `runtimeSessionId`, alert on `reconnected: true` and on `4000` evictions, and record that command content is structurally uncollectable from AWS-native logs — it can only be recovered from the harness runtime itself

findings.title: Claude Compliance Activity Feed retroactively strips file names, document names and artifact titles
findings.description: As of **September 24**, the Compliance API's Activity Feed no longer returns `filename` or `title` on file, project-document and artifact activities. The fields are **"now always empty or omitted, including on activities recorded before this change"** — this is not a going-forward change, it silently degrades **already-collected history**. Resolving a name from the ID on the activity now requires a **separate Compliance Access Key scoped `read:compliance_user_data`**, which is a different (and more sensitive) credential than the feed itself needs. Any Zenity detection, DLP correlation or investigation workflow that matched on document names in the Activity Feed is now matching on empty strings and will **fail silently rather than error**. AIDR must (a) treat empty `filename`/`title` as "redacted," not "no file," (b) add the ID→name lookup as a second collection step with its own credential, and (c) re-check whether any existing rule keys on these fields. This is a coverage regression rather than a new feature, reported because it directly reduces an active detection surface

findings.title: AgentCore `inline_function` tools execute client-side, and the obvious audit hook is documented as unreliable for them
findings.description: An `inline_function` tool is defined with a schema on the harness but **"executes on the client side, not on the harness VM."** The harness pauses with `stopReason: "tool_use"`, hands the call back to the caller's code, and resumes only when a matching `toolResult` arrives on the same `runtimeSessionId`. AWS names **human-in-the-loop approvals** as the primary pattern — meaning the approval gate for an agent's most sensitive actions frequently lives entirely outside AWS, in customer code, with no AWS-side record of what was approved or by whom. The harness holds the authoritative `toolUse` in session state and ignores a resent copy; a missing, duplicate, stale or replayed result cannot resume the handoff. AWS further warns to read the lifecycle-hooks caveat **"before using an `after_tool_call` event for an inline function as an authorization or audit signal"** — the natural instrumentation point is explicitly not trustworthy for this tool type. AISPM should inventory `inline_function` tools separately from server-side tools, record that their execution and any approval decision are off-platform, and flag harnesses whose privileged actions are gated only by an inline function

platforms.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (tier: primary) — carried audit debt cleared
details: **Harness persistent filesystem mounts.** A harness can mount three distinct persistent filesystem types at paths under `/mnt`: service-managed **session storage** (survives stop/resume for a `runtimeSessionId`, no VPC needed), an **Amazon EFS access point** (customer-owned, explicitly "shared across sessions and agents", up to 2 mounts, VPC required), and an **Amazon S3 Files access point** (up to 2 mounts, VPC required) whose mount path **syncs bidirectionally with the backing S3 bucket**. Files written to these mounts survive session termination and are visible to later invocations. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness-environment.html

**`InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` — direct root shell into the harness microVM.** AWS documents this as deliberate out-of-band access: "deterministic command execution with no model reasoning, no token cost." Commands run as **root (uid 0)**, and AWS states plainly that a `USER` directive in the customer's Dockerfile "applies to the agent process only" — `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` "runs at a higher privilege level," and "the IAM permission is the access gate, not the in-VM privilege level." Documented uses include cloning repos, installing packages, and pushing commits. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness-environment.html

**Harness memory: caller-supplied `actorId` is the isolation boundary, and managed memory is provisioned by default.** Memory events are scoped by `actorId` + `sessionId`, and `actorId` is passed by the caller on each `InvokeHarness` call. Long-term retrieval templates `actorId` directly into namespace paths (e.g. `/summary/{actorId}/{sessionId}/`). Retrieval is automatic on every invocation (`topK=10`, `relevanceScore=0.2` by default) and injects retrieved memories into context before the model reasons. Separately: creating a harness through the **service API** with the memory configuration omitted causes the service to **provision managed memory automatically** (the CLI defaults the other way, to disabled), and `DeleteHarness` cascade-deletes it unless `deleteManagedMemory=false`. BYO memory can be attached to and shared across multiple harnesses. Four long-term strategies: `SEMANTIC`, `SUMMARIZATION`, `USER_PREFERENCE`, `EPISODIC`. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness-memory.html

**Harness skill sources — four source types, fully enumerated.** The `skills` field (settable at create time, overridable per invocation, invoke-time entries appended after and winning on name collision) accepts: `awsSkills` (pre-built AWS-service skills from the AWS Agent Toolkit, glob-selected), `git` (clone **any public or private HTTPS Git repository**, sparse-checkout a subdirectory, private repos authenticated via a Token Vault `apikeycredentialprovider` ARN), `s3` (customer bucket, fetched with the execution role, ≤1 GB), and `path` (filesystem, baked into the container image *or installed at session start via `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand`*). Skills follow the open **AgentSkills.io** standard — a `SKILL.md` plus optional `scripts/`, `references/` and `assets/` directories. Skills are fetched once per session and persist on disk across invocations. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness-skills.html

platforms.name: Cursor (tier: watching)
details: **`cursor.com/docs/rollouts` now exists** (404 on the 2026-09-24 scan). The docs page materially **corrects** the changelog text this report relied on yesterday: Rollouts **does not automatically revert** — on a detected regression it "opens an issue, and notifies the author." It also documents the real integration surface: up to **200 monitored repositories**; version control across **GitHub, GitLab.com, Bitbucket Cloud and Origin**; observability via **Datadog and other tools connected over MCP**; Slack notifications to a DM or channel; and CI/CD integration by placing a **Cursor API key in CI secrets**. platforms.name: OpenAI Codex (tier: primary)
details: **Codex CLI 0.157.0 (2026-09-25)** — "Enabled automatic background-server startup for eligible interactive sessions, with recovery choices when server settings are incompatible"; "Made `/import` available in remote sessions and local background-server sessions"; an `f` shortcut to "fork conversations open in another app, preserving drafts and queued prompts"; GPT-6 Sol and Luna added to the catalog including **Amazon Bedrock** as a provider. Source: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/changelog

findings.title: AgentCore harness persistent filesystem mounts — three new resource types, one explicitly cross-agent
findings.description: A harness can mount service-managed session storage, up to two **EFS access points**, and up to two **S3 Files access points** at paths under `/mnt`. AWS states the EFS mount is "shared across sessions and agents" — meaning two different agents, potentially with different execution roles and different data-classification levels, can be wired to the same access point and exchange files outside any modelled data flow. The S3 Files mount **syncs bidirectionally**, so anything an agent writes to its local mount path lands in the customer's S3 bucket automatically, and anything placed in that bucket becomes agent-readable input. Zenity's AgentCore inventory must add `filesystemConfigurations` as a first-class relationship — mapping each harness to its `sessionStorage`, `efsAccessPoint` and `s3FilesAccessPoint` mounts — and AISPM should raise a toxic-combination finding when one EFS or S3 Files access point is mounted by more than one agent or harness, and when an S3 Files-backed bucket is also writable by a non-agent principal (an injection path into agent context). Note `UpdateHarness` replaces the entire `filesystemConfigurations` list, so mount changes are not incremental and a drift-detection baseline must re-read the whole list

findings.title: `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` executes arbitrary shell as root inside the agent's microVM, bypassing the agent loop entirely
findings.description: AWS documents this API as a deliberate out-of-band path with "no model reasoning, no token cost" — meaning it produces **no agent turn, no tool-use event and no model trace**. Commands run as **uid 0** regardless of a `USER` directive in the customer's container image, and AWS is explicit that "the IAM permission is the access gate, not the in-VM privilege level." The documented use cases are themselves high-impact: clone a repository, install dependencies, run tests, **commit and push**, extract build artifacts, and install skills into `.agents/skills/` at session start. Any AIDR model that infers agent activity from invocation traces or model telemetry will see nothing at all for this path. Zenity must treat `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` as a distinct high-severity activity type sourced from CloudTrail rather than from agent traces, and AISPM must flag any principal holding it — it is effectively root on the agent host, and it is a separate IAM action from `InvokeHarness`

findings.title: Harness memory isolation depends on a caller-supplied `actorId` string
findings.description: Short-term and long-term memory are scoped by `actorId` + `sessionId`, and `actorId` is an ordinary request field the caller sets on `InvokeHarness`. Long-term retrieval templates it straight into the namespace path (`/summary/{actorId}/{sessionId}/`) and runs **automatically on every invocation**, injecting the top 10 semantically-matched records into context before the model reasons. If the calling application forwards a client-controlled identifier — or if the caller is a SigV4 principal, which per the harness security page gets **no per-user identity propagation at all** — then submitting another user's `actorId` retrieves that user's extracted facts, summaries, preferences and episodes into the attacker's session. This is a cross-tenant memory read reachable with no IAM change, and the injected content is also an indirect prompt-injection carrier (it is written by prior conversations). AIRT should add a probe that varies `actorId` across otherwise identical sessions and checks for retrieval leakage; AISPM should flag harnesses that are both memory-enabled and SigV4-invoked

findings.title: AgentCore harness managed memory is silently auto-provisioned by the service API
findings.description: Creating a harness through the service API with the memory configuration **omitted** causes AgentCore to provision a managed AgentCore Memory resource automatically — the AgentCore CLI defaults the opposite way (disabled). The result is a persistent store of conversation events and extracted long-term records (`SEMANTIC`, `SUMMARIZATION`, `USER_PREFERENCE`, `EPISODIC` strategies) that exists without the operator ever asking for it, and which cannot be deleted through the Memory APIs directly. Zenity's inventory must not assume "no memory configured" means "no memory" — it must resolve each harness's effective memory resource and mark implicitly-provisioned managed memory as an undeclared data store. Conversely, `DeleteHarness` cascade-deletes that memory by default unless `deleteManagedMemory=false` is passed, which matters for evidence retention. BYO memory attached to several harnesses is an additional cross-agent data-sharing edge to model

findings.title: AgentCore harness skill sources — four source types including arbitrary Git clone at invoke time
findings.description: This supplies the concrete entity model behind the per-invocation skill-override risk reported on 2026-09-24. The `skills` field accepts `awsSkills` (glob-selected AWS Agent Toolkit skills granting EC2/S3/Lambda/DynamoDB/CloudWatch/**IAM** operational knowledge), `git` (any public or private HTTPS repository, private repos authenticated with a Token Vault API-key credential provider holding a PAT), `s3` (execution-role-fetched, ≤1 GB), and `path` (baked into the image, or installed mid-session via `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand`). Skills carry a `scripts/` directory alongside `SKILL.md` and conform to the open **AgentSkills.io** specification — the same cross-vendor plugin format Zenity already tracks — so a skill bundle is executable content, not just prose. Zenity should inventory skill attachments as a per-harness entity with the source type, URI/repo, and credential ARN recorded; flag invoke-time overrides as distinct from create-time defaults (invoke-time wins on name collision); and flag `awsSkills` globs that pull in IAM-operation skills

findings.title: Codex CLI 0.157.0 starts a background server by default and opens `/import` to remote and background-server sessions
findings.description: As of 0.157.0 the Codex CLI "enable[s] automatic background-server startup for eligible interactive sessions" — a long-lived local listener now comes up without the user opting in — and `/import` (pulling external content into a session) is newly available **in remote sessions and in local background-server sessions**. A new `f` shortcut forks a conversation that is open in another application, carrying over drafts and queued prompts, which moves conversation state across process boundaries. For endpoint coverage this means Codex's local footprint is no longer bounded by a foreground TUI process: ENDPOINT must detect the background server, and treat `/import` in a background-server session as an untrusted-content ingestion point into a tool-capable local agent

platforms.name: Cursor (tier: watching)
details: **Rollouts** — a new production-monitoring bot. It attaches a monitor to every pull request, reads the diff and the systems it touches, and writes a monitoring plan as a PR comment. It wakes on deploy events for the change's commit and runs that plan against the customer's logs, metrics and traces, tracking each environment separately and returning a per-environment verdict (verified healthy / regression detected / inconclusive). On a regression it names the suspected change, notifies the author, and — depending on configuration — **opens a revert PR or hands the finding to a cloud agent for a fix**. Integrations: source control (GitHub/Origin), the customer's CD system, and telemetry providers including Datadog, Grafana and Honeycomb. Teams and Enterprise plans. Source: https://cursor.com/changelog/rollouts-and-security-reviewer

**Security Review** — a new security-agent family shipped alongside Rollouts. *Security Reviewer* reads every pull request in the context of the whole codebase and posts a single review comment reporting exploitable bugs (SQL/command/template injection, authn/authz bypass, secrets and credentials, SSRF, unsafe deserialization, vulnerable dependencies). A companion *Vulnerability Scanner* scans the codebase **at rest** for pre-existing issues. Teams can add custom codebase rules. Enabled per repository from the dashboard; draft PRs excluded. Source: https://cursor.com/docs/security-agents

platforms.name: Google Gemini Enterprise (tier: secondary)
details: **D&B Finance Analytics data store (Public Preview)** — new third-party data store. Beyond read access to company and credit reports, scores, filings and corporate ownership, it **supports actions**: creating and processing credit applications, and managing folders. This is the fifth connector-action expansion since 2026-08-21 and the second D&B data store in three days (D&B Risk Analytics GA'd 2026-09-22). Source: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/connectors/d-and-b-commercial-graph

platforms.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (tier: primary) — carried audit debt cleared
details: **Caller-controlled model configuration and skill sources.** The `model.additionalParams`, `apiBase` and `modelId` fields on `InvokeHarness` are passed through to the model provider **unvalidated and unfiltered** by AWS. The `skills` field can be overridden per invocation to point the harness at arbitrary S3 or Git sources, and the harness "treats all skill content as trusted input." Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness-security.html

**Harness IAM permission model and `harness-endpoint` resource type.** Harness APIs require paired permissions on both the harness ARN and the underlying AgentCore Runtime (and Memory) resource — e.g. `InvokeHarness` needs both `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeHarness` and `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime`. A distinct `arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:<region>:<account>:harness/<id>/harness-endpoint/<name>` resource type exists with its own Create/Update/Delete/Get/List actions. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness-security.html

platforms.name: Cognition Devin Desktop (tier: watching)
details: **v3.10.35 (2026-09-24): MCP servers advertised by ACP clients are now usable inside Devin sessions.** An MCP server the user never configured in Devin can now be reached by a Devin agent because a connected ACP (Agent Client Protocol) client exposes it. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/changelog

findings.title: Cursor Rollouts — an AI agent with production deploy, telemetry and revert authority
findings.description: A new Cursor bot that attaches to every PR, ingests the customer's production logs, metrics and traces via Datadog/Grafana/Honeycomb integrations, and can autonomously open revert PRs or delegate a fix to a cloud agent. This introduces new inventory entities Zenity does not model: Rollouts monitors (one per PR), per-environment change-health verdicts, CD-system connections, and telemetry-provider connections. The toxic combination is concrete — an agent holding simultaneous read access to production observability data and write access to the source repository, able to revert code with no human in the loop depending on configuration. AISPM must discover Rollouts enablement per org, enumerate its connected deploy and telemetry providers, and flag configurations where autonomous revert is enabled

findings.title: Cursor Security Agents — Security Reviewer and Vulnerability Scanner
findings.description: A new agent family that reads every pull request *in the context of the entire codebase* and, via the Vulnerability Scanner, scans the codebase at rest. New inventory entities: Security Reviewer agent configurations, per-repository enablement, custom codebase rules, and at-rest scan results. The security-relevant property is that these agents ingest whole-repository content — including secrets they are explicitly tasked with finding — and emit findings into PR comments, creating a new data-flow path out of the codebase. AISPM must inventory which repositories have security agents enabled and what custom rules are attached

findings.title: AgentCore harness accepts unvalidated model configuration and caller-supplied skill sources
findings.description: AWS documents that `additionalParams`, `apiBase` and `modelId` on `InvokeHarness` are passed to the model provider without validation. A caller can use LiteLLM's `aws_bedrock_runtime_endpoint` to redirect the signed request — **including the SigV4 signature and session credentials** — to an attacker-chosen endpoint, use OpenAI's `extra_headers` to override the `Authorization` header, attempt role escalation via `aws_role_name` + `sts:AssumeRole`, or redirect inference to a different model, region or provider entirely. Separately, the `skills` field can be overridden per invocation to fetch arbitrary markdown and scripts from any S3 bucket or Git repo, which the harness injects into agent context as trusted instructions. Both are first-class prompt-injection and credential-exfiltration vectors reachable by any principal that passes the IAM/JWT gate. AIRT should add probes for `additionalParams` endpoint redirection and per-invocation skill-source override; AISPM should flag harnesses whose execution role grants `sts:AssumeRole` or whose application forwards caller-supplied `model` and `skills` fields

findings.title: AgentCore `harness-endpoint` resource type and paired-permission IAM model
findings.description: A distinct resource type `arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:<region>:<account>:harness/<id>/harness-endpoint/<endpointName>` exists with its own `CreateHarnessEndpoint` / `UpdateHarnessEndpoint` / `DeleteHarnessEndpoint` / `GetHarnessEndpoint` / `ListHarnessEndpoints` actions, plus `ListHarnessVersions`. Harness control-plane calls require paired permissions on the harness *and* the underlying Runtime and Memory resources, meaning a principal appearing to hold only harness permissions may in fact carry Runtime and Memory authority. Zenity's AgentCore inventory must add `harness-endpoint` as an entity and model the paired-permission expansion when computing effective agent privilege. Note also that SigV4 callers do **not** get per-user identity propagation into downstream tool calls — only inbound OAuth (Bearer JWT) does — so any SigV4-invoked harness runs downstream tools under a shared service identity

findings.title: Gemini Enterprise D&B Finance Analytics data store with write actions
findings.description: New Public Preview connector giving agents natural-language access to company and credit reports, scores, filings and corporate ownership, and — critically — **write actions** that create and process credit applications and manage folders. New inventory entities: the D&B Finance Analytics data store, its connector-action set, and the credit-application objects it can create. An agent with this connector can originate financial transactions, not merely read reference data. AISPM must discover the data store and enumerate its granted actions. **Doc gap:** Google has published no per-store page for either D&B store; the shared D&B connector overview does not enumerate actions, auth model or entity types, so the action set needs a follow-up sweep once documentation lands

findings.title: Devin Desktop exposes ACP-client MCP servers inside agent sessions
findings.description: As of v3.10.35, MCP servers advertised by a connected ACP (Agent Client Protocol) client are usable from within Devin Desktop sessions. This is a transitive MCP-tool surface: a local agent gains tools that were never registered in Devin's own configuration, so an endpoint inventory built from Devin's MCP config alone will under-report the agent's real tool set. ENDPOINT coverage must resolve MCP servers reachable through ACP clients, not only those declared locally

platforms.name: Claude Enterprise (Anthropic)
details: **Inline tool definitions — `tool_addition` by value (`inline-tools-2026-09-15` beta, September 22)** — a `tool_addition` block in a mid-conversation `role: "system"` message can now carry a **full tool definition by value** (name, description, `input_schema`) rather than naming a tool that was already declared in the request's `tools` array. The `tools` array never changes, so the prompt cache still hits. Re-sending a definition under the same name **replaces the tool's schema from that point onward**. Combined with the `mcp-client-2026-09-15` beta header, the same block can attach an **`mcp_toolset`** mid-conversation, and the response then carries `mcp_tool_listing` blocks enumerating that server's tools. Limits: 10,000 deferred tools, 10,000 tools defined after the first user message, 4 MB of post-first-user-message tool definitions. Computer-use tools cannot be defined inline. Supported on Claude Fable 5.1, Mythos 5.1, Opus 5, Opus 5.5 — on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages

**Claude Opus 5.5 (September 22)** — `claude-opus-5-5`, 1M context, 128k max output, always-on adaptive thinking; `thinking: {"type":"disabled"}` and `tool_choice` `any`/`tool` return 400. Computer use requires the `computer_toolset_20260801` toolset. Fast mode available as a research preview. *Model-inventory watchlist item; not raised as a coverage finding.* Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/api

platforms.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
details: **Harness: Interactive shells (terminals)** — `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell` opens a persistent, interactive **Bash PTY over WebSocket** inside the microVM running a harness session, at `wss://bedrock-agentcore.<region>.amazonaws.com/runtimes/<harness-arn>/ws/shells`. Environment variables, working directory, command history and running processes persist across inputs. A client can detach and **reconnect with the stored `shellId`**, replaying up to 256 KB of buffered output; up to **10 concurrent shells** per harness session (20 retained active+detached entries), 1-hour connection cap, 64 KB frames, 250 frames/sec. Auth is SigV4 (`bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell`), a SigV4 pre-signed URL, or a bearer token accepted by the harness inbound authorizer — including a **browser-friendly base64url bearer token passed through `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`**. Works in the managed default environment and in a configured custom container. AWS's own guidance: the shell "can access customer-provided data, files, and secrets in the selected environment or on mounted filesystems" and "connect to network destinations that the session can reach." **CloudTrail records the API call and CloudWatch gets connection metadata, but neither logs terminal input or output.** Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness-command-shell.html

platforms.name: ChatGPT Enterprise (OpenAI)
details: **Codex CLI 0.156.0 (September 22)** — fullscreen TUI with search; **voice conversations enabled by default with bundled runtimes**; a **usage analytics dashboard at `/usage`** with plan history tracking; **daemon update management via `/daemon`**; worktree session filtering; **Windows sandbox changes — network policy support, DNS resolution, account handling, and integration with managed proxy routing**; **MCP policy consistency enforcement** and improved MCP credential handling; Code Mode tool metadata improvements and filesystem accessor bindings; refactored Guardian reviewer lifecycle; Mermaid/equation rendering. Source: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/changelog

**GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna (September 22)** — new models in the API, Codex and ChatGPT Work, at ~50% lower API pricing than GPT-5.6; selectable from the Codex model picker as of CLI 0.156.1 (September 23). Follows GPT-6 Astra, already on the watchlist from the 2026-09-18 report. *Model-inventory watchlist item; not raised as a coverage finding.* Source: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/changelog

platforms.name: Google Gemini Enterprise
details: **D&B Risk Analytics data store — GA (September 22)** — a second Dun & Bradstreet federated data store alongside D&B Commercial Graph, targeted at KYB onboarding, counterparty due diligence, sanctions screening and risk assessment. It is a **connector with actions**, not a read-only index; Google's own guidance is to associate only one data store with the actions belonging to a single connector type. Available in `global`, `us` and `eu`; VPC Service Controls enforcement requires deleting and recreating existing data stores. Source: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/connectors/d-and-b-commercial-graph

findings.title: Anthropic inline tool definitions — tools and MCP servers introduced mid-conversation, by value
findings.description: A `tool_addition` block in a `role: "system"` message can now carry a complete tool definition, so a tool that Claude will call **need never appear in the request's `tools` array**. Every static analysis Zenity performs that reads an agent's declared toolset from the top of the request is now incomplete by design: the real tool surface is the union of `tools` plus every inline definition appended across the conversation, and a later definition under the same name **silently replaces the earlier schema**. Two consequences compound this. First, the same mechanism can attach an entire **`mcp_toolset` mid-conversation** (with `mcp-client-2026-09-15`), which means an MCP server — and the arbitrary tool list it returns in `mcp_tool_listing` — can enter an agent's reach after the conversation started and after any pre-flight policy check ran. Second, because the system-message block is *appended data*, an agent pipeline that builds messages from retrieved or user-influenced content gives an injection a route to **define its own tool** rather than merely persuade the model to misuse an existing one. AIRT needs probes for inline tool injection and mid-conversation MCP attachment; AISPM must treat an agent's tool inventory as conversation-scoped and evolving, parse `tool_addition` and `mcp_tool_listing` blocks as first-class inventory events, and alert on schema replacement of an already-known tool name

findings.title: AgentCore harness interactive shells (`InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell`)
findings.description: A new WebSocket API that gives a caller a persistent, stateful Bash terminal inside the microVM running a harness agent — the same environment as the agent, with the same filesystem, mounted secrets and network reachability. AWS states plainly that **terminal input and output are not logged**: CloudTrail captures only the fact of the `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell` call (caller identity, timestamp, source IP, resolved runtime, response status), and CloudWatch receives connection metadata only. Everything typed and everything returned is invisible to AWS-native logging, which makes this the least-observed execution path AgentCore has shipped. Detach-and-reconnect (`shellId` + runtime session ID) means a process started in one connection keeps running unattended and can be resumed later from a different client, and the browser-oriented **base64url bearer token over `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`** path means a shell can be opened from a browser without SigV4 at all, authorised only by the harness inbound authorizer. Zenity must inventory which principals hold `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell` and on which harness ARNs, treat any grant of it as a high-privilege finding (AWS's own security note says to restrict it to trusted principals and specific harness ARNs), surface harnesses whose inbound authorizer would accept a bearer-token shell connection, and ingest the CloudTrail event as an AIDR activity type — with the explicit caveat that content-level detection is not available and the compensating control has to be authorisation, not inspection

findings.title: Codex CLI 0.156.0 — always-on voice with bundled runtimes, a local usage dashboard, and managed proxy routing in the Windows sandbox
findings.description: Three changes alter what Codex is on a workstation. **Voice conversations are now enabled by default and ship with bundled runtimes**, which turns the local coding agent into a always-available microphone-driven input path with its own embedded speech runtime on disk — a new prompt-entry vector that leaves no text artifact and a new bundled binary to inventory. The **`/usage` analytics dashboard with plan history** is a locally reachable record of the agent's own consumption; useful as telemetry, and also a reconnaissance surface. The Windows sandbox now carries **network policy support, DNS resolution and integration with managed proxy routing**, meaning Codex's egress on Windows is governed by a configurable local policy object that ENDPOINT should read and assess rather than assume. Alongside these, **MCP policy consistency enforcement** and improved MCP credential handling change how locally configured MCP servers are admitted, and **Code Mode tool metadata plus filesystem accessor bindings** expand what the agent can reach on the filesystem. This is an extension of the Codex daemon/worktree endpoint object already reported 2026-09-18, not a new product, hence MEDIUM

findings.title: Gemini Enterprise D&B Risk Analytics data store (GA)
findings.description: A second Dun & Bradstreet connector reaches GA, and unlike a plain search index it is a **connector with actions** — meaning a Gemini Enterprise agent can invoke operations against an external commercial-risk service, not merely read from it. The declared use cases (KYB onboarding, counterparty due diligence, sanctions screening, risk decisioning) put it directly in a regulated decision path: an agent grounded on this store is producing outputs that feed onboarding and credit decisions, and the store itself becomes a route by which internal counterparty identifiers leave the tenant for a third-party data provider. AISPM must add D&B Risk Analytics as an inventory entity alongside D&B Commercial Graph, enumerate the actions registered for it (the action set is the privilege, not the connector), capture its region binding (`global`/`us`/`eu`) as a data-residency attribute, and flag agents that hold it as a grounding source in a compliance-relevant workflow

platforms.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
details: **Harness: Lifecycle hooks** — hooks fire at `before_invocation`, `before_tool_call`, `after_tool_call` and `after_invocation`, including for inline-function tool calls. An AWS Lambda target returns a synchronous `allow` or `deny` that can stop an invocation or skip a tool call; Amazon SNS and Amazon EventBridge targets receive non-blocking notifications. `InvokeHarness` emits a `hookEvent` for each configured hook that fires. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness-lifecycle-hooks.html

**Harness: Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints** — OpenAI model configurations now accept an optional `apiBase` field, routing direct OpenAI requests through a customer-specified gateway, proxy, self-hosted endpoint or regional endpoint. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness-models.html

platforms.name: Claude Enterprise (Anthropic)
details: **Life Sciences Verification Program (September 17, 2026)** — a vetting-gated entitlement that replaces an organisation's biology-related safety classifiers with a more permissive set. Two tiers: *Standard Use* (Mythos, Opus and Sonnet with classifiers tuned permissive for science tasks) and *High-risk Use*, an add-on that **removes all safeguards blocking life-sciences requests** for a named project. Cyber classifiers and other safeguards are retained. Grants are annual (Standard) or bi-annual (High-risk), scoped to declared use cases, and enforcement shifts from real-time blocking to offline pattern analysis. Source: https://www.anthropic.com/news/life-sciences-verification-program

platforms.name: Google Gemini Enterprise
details: **Transfer agent ownership (September 21, 2026)** — administrators holding `roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceAdmin` or `roles/discoveryengine.admin` can reassign ownership of a shared agent to another user, including themselves. Shared agents only; the new owner becomes sole owner and the previous owner is downgraded to `agentUser`. Targets may be Google accounts or Workforce Identity Federation principals. Any schedule or event trigger on the agent is marked disabled by the transfer and must be re-enabled by the new owner. Source: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/share-custom-agents

findings.title: AgentCore harness lifecycle hooks
findings.description: A new synchronous interception and control surface inside the AgentCore agent loop. Four hook points (`before_invocation`, `before_tool_call`, `after_tool_call`, `after_invocation`) can each bind a Lambda that returns `allow`/`deny` and can halt an invocation or suppress a tool call, plus SNS/EventBridge fan-out targets. This introduces new inventory entities (harness hook configurations, their Lambda/SNS/EventBridge targets) and a new activity type — the `hookEvent` records emitted by `InvokeHarness` — which is a first-class detection feed for what an AgentCore agent actually invoked. It is also a control plane an attacker with harness-config write access can neuter or repurpose: replacing a `deny` Lambda silently removes the customer's own tool-call gating, and a `before_tool_call` Lambda sees every tool argument, making it an exfiltration point. Zenity must inventory hook configurations, alert on hooks removed or repointed, and ingest `hookEvent` as an AIDR activity source

findings.title: Anthropic Life Sciences Verification Program — entitlement-based safeguard removal
findings.description: A verified organisation's Claude deployment can run with biology safety classifiers relaxed (Standard Use) or, at the High-risk tier, with all life-sciences-blocking safeguards removed for a named project. Guardrail behaviour is therefore a property of the *entitlement attached to the workspace/API key*, not of the model — the same `claude-mythos-5`/Opus/Sonnet model ID behaves differently for an entitled org, and Anthropic explicitly moves that tier from real-time blocking to offline pattern analysis. Red-team probes that infer safety posture from refusals will pass falsely against an entitled deployment. AIRT needs a bio-domain probe set, and AISPM needs to record the LSVP entitlement and tier as a property of the Anthropic connection so an unexpected High-risk grant is a finding. Directly parallels the Mythos-5 safeguard-lifting pattern already tracked

findings.title: AgentCore harness custom OpenAI endpoint (`apiBase`)
findings.description: OpenAI model configs in the AgentCore harness now take an `apiBase` pointing at any OpenAI-compatible gateway, proxy, self-hosted or regional endpoint. This is a new outbound model-traffic path that leaves AWS-observed inference entirely — every prompt, tool result and completion for that agent can be routed to an arbitrary third-party host set by a single config field, with no code change and no new IAM resource. AISPM must surface `apiBase` per harness configuration, treat a non-default value as an unmonitored data-egress edge, and flag agents whose model traffic bypasses Bedrock

findings.title: Gemini Enterprise agent ownership transfer
findings.description: A new administrative action that reassigns the sole owner of a shared agent, demoting the previous owner to `agentUser`, and that accepts Workforce Identity Federation principals as well as Google accounts. This mutates an inventory relationship Zenity already models (agent → owner) through a path that is not agent creation, so ownership drift will go unobserved unless the transfer is tracked; it is also a plausible privilege-consolidation move — an admin can make themselves the owner of any shared agent in the tenant. The transfer additionally disables the agent's schedule and event triggers, silently changing autonomous-execution posture. AISPM should treat owner change on an existing agent, and trigger-state change caused by it, as distinct monitored events
